log.why: E9 tests three genes with combined prior 0.427, roughly bisecting the probability mass for maximum information gain.
Treating at 10 µM splits the prior probability mass nearly in half (0.481 vs 0.519), maximizing information gain for Ticket 2.
E9 narrowed the culprit to katG, hisG, or gyrA; testing top candidate hisG (0.403) directly can confirm it for immediate publication.
Treat at 3 uM to split the probability mass between thresholds <= 3 uM (0.48) and 10 uM (0.41).
Knocking out katG directly tests the leading hypothesis (0.489) and clearly separates it from gyrA (0.276).
With response at 10 uM and none at 3 uM, the 0.721 posterior for 10 uM justifies publishing now and freeing a ticket slot.
Test gyrA directly on Ticket 1 since it has 0.490 posterior and only 34s remaining.
While waiting for Ticket 1's E2, bisect Ticket 3's hypotheses using E10 (combined prior 0.535).
Ticket 1 will expire too soon to test; testing top candidate lacZ (0.422) on Ticket 3 maximizes information before its deadline.
With only 23s left on Ticket 3, starting E1 (katG) now hedges against E2 being negative while leaving time to publish.
Ticket 3 has only 5 seconds left and a strong 0.937 posterior for lacZ.
Testing {rpoB, trpE} splits the Ticket 5 posterior in half (0.508 vs 0.492) for maximum information gain.
E9 ({rpoB, lacZ, gyrA}) is orthogonal to the growing E5 ({rpoB, trpE}), allowing us to pinpoint the top candidates in one step.
Test gyrA directly on Ticket 5 to distinguish it from lacZ before time runs out.
With 13s left in the round, publishing recA (0.324) has positive expected value and finishes just as Ticket 5's E4 completes.
